title: Fewest Lamps To Light Corridor
description:
## Task

A corridor runs from position 0 to position `n`, where `n` is one less than the length of `reach`. There is a lamp socket at every integer position `i`, and a lamp placed at socket `i` lights every position from `i - reach[i]` to `i + reach[i]`, both included (a reach of 0 lights only its own position). Switch on as few lamps as possible so that the whole corridor from 0 to `n` is lit, with no dark gaps between lit positions.

## Input

- `reach` — a list of non-negative integers, one per socket; its length is `n + 1`.

## Output

The smallest number of lamps that light every position from 0 to `n`. (Every socket lights at least itself, so a full cover always exists.) Trying subsets of lamps is hopeless on the big inputs; a linear or n log n method is expected.

## Example

```python
fewest_lamps([3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0])  # returns 4
fewest_lamps([1, 4, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 2, 0])  # returns 2
fewest_lamps([0])  # returns 1
```

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ length of `reach` ≤ 5·10^4
- 0 ≤ each value ≤ 5·10^4
